# TransferEncodingWithContentLength

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Choose a single HTTP message framing mechanism.

## Example

Finding:

```php{2}
<?php
header("Transfer-Encoding: chunked"); header("Content-Length: 12");
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Choose a single HTTP message framing mechanism.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Track effective Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length headers set by builtin header in the same straight-line response segment. Report the second header establishing both. Header replacement and header_remove update state; either order is supported.
- Emit one finding per violating operation. Flow facts require a reachable path with no intervening mutation, escaped alias, unknown call involving the tracked value or analysis-budget exhaustion. Uncertain facts cannot prove a violation.

## Exceptions (no report)

- A removal before the second header and unknown/branch-dependent header state are excluded. This rule checks HTTP/1.1 sender framing; manually setting Transfer-Encoding for other protocols is not legitimized.
- Exclude shadowed builtin symbols, unresolved required types, incomplete syntax and unsupported PHP versions.

## Fix

No automatic fix. Choosing a repair requires runtime information, error-handling policy or a semantic decision.

All edits use exact byte ranges, preserve comments and evaluation order, and require syntax supported by the target PHP version. A fix must never add an evaluation or silently change unrelated arguments.

## PHP versions

Available throughout PHP 5.3–8.5.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "TransferEncodingWithContentLength": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore TransferEncodingWithContentLength
```
